experiences.title: Wafer feature → screened dies → accepted assembly

model.identityScope: File hashes identify this exact integrated snapshot. A version label alone does not prove an unchanged implementation.

experiences.scope: A linked synthetic wafer-feature slice and input-to-assembly accounting exercise. It is not a complete transistor process, TCAD solution, modern manufacturing recipe or real qualification record.
assumptions: Thickness, CD, spatial variation, uncertainty half-widths, specification limits and every survival input are authored teaching values. Silicon consumption uses an illustrative 0.44 ratio, not a value established by the cited theoretical excerpt.

Prescribed oxide and deposited poly-Si films, latent positive resist, development and ideal vertical transfer are separate stages. Finite selectivity consumes mask; geometric section drawings are schematic.
Deterministic uncertainty-interval containment distinguishes pass, boundary review and failure. It is not probabilistic risk analysis or standard compliance.

Grid-fit gross dies, geometric-screened dies, a Poisson zero-defect fraction and screened inputs have separate denominators. Packages consume two screened dies and eight already-accepted HBM stacks; conditional assembly survival is applied once.
Electrical/mechanical interface example checks and qualification evidence are separate from geometric overlap. Pending qualification cannot become accepted output.

experiences.title: Bit address → bank state → stack interface → working set

model.identityScope: File hashes identify this exact integrated snapshot. A version label alone does not prove an unchanged implementation.

experiences.scope: A synthetic logical address and bank-command explorer linked to the existing atlas stack and inference byte-accounting models. It reveals no vendor physical address layout, calibrated joint reliability or device timing.
assumptions: Each die exposes a two-GiB binary teaching window; the existing model uses three decimal GB per die. Unmapped bytes remain usable capacity, not defective memory. Stack selection is separate from byte addressing.
The declared byte/bit, column, bank, pseudo-channel, channel, row and die fields are synthetic. Closed-bank, open-row-hit and conflicting-row command order has no refresh or timing model.
Stack dimensions, capacity, thermal path and working-set totals reuse reference-system/investigation models through memoryContextFromAtlas; no second set of hardware constants replaces them.

Free thermal mismatch is a CGA-inspired global geometric analogy. Displacement/gap applies only to solder-bearing routes; hybrid has no solder shear value. It predicts neither local stress nor fatigue lifetime.
Already-screened inputs, post-bond test, geometry and explicit qualification remain distinct. A missing qualification record cannot produce accepted example stacks.

HBF holds read-only weights by teaching policy; mutable KV, staging workspace, static placement and next-step append headroom are separate. The transfer ledger does not double-count persistent inventory.

experiences.title: One exact matrix product across four organizations

model.identityScope: File hashes identify this exact integrated snapshot. A version label alone does not prove an unchanged implementation.

experiences.scope: Exact bounded integer C=AB under four authored scalar, vector, SIMT and systolic schedules. Logical movement and partial outputs illustrate organization without a measured speed ranking.
assumptions: C starts at zero; square 2×2 or 3×3 matrices use integer entries −99…99. Required arithmetic remains n³ MACs across organizations.
Two, four or eight teaching slots are not CUDA warp widths. Excluded slots explicitly remap mathematical work; actual masking alone would not compute omitted outputs.
Issue slots and wavefront ticks are not comparable physical clock durations. Cache behavior, coalescing, divergence, resident-warp occupancy, pipeline hazards and instruction timing are excluded.
Traffic counts logical boundary/local accesses and PE neighbor hops, not HBM transactions. Systolic output-stationary tiling, skew and one-tick neighbor transfer are original teaching choices.

experiences.title: Arithmetic contract → mapped netlist → placed FPGA artifact

model.identityScope: File hashes identify this exact integrated snapshot. A version label alone does not prove an unchanged implementation.

experiences.scope: An actual public-tool FPGA synthesis/place-and-route artifact for a bounded adder, plus mapped LUT/register execution. Tool artifacts are primary run evidence; documentation source checks are separately inventoried.
assumptions: Unsigned four-bit a + b produces five-bit q. Rising edge n captures the sum of the input sample at n−1; power-on fill is unspecified.
Target is iCE40HX1K/TQ144, seed 7 and an internal 100 MHz target. Reported fmax is a tool timing-model result; IOs are automatically assigned without board constraints.
Browser register fill is zero only for inspection; hardware power-on state is unspecified. Only the filled output contract is asserted.
Yosys SAT covers the combinational contract. Icarus runs all 256 operand pairs against RTL and mapped primitives. These software checks are not human review or physical measurement.
Actual FPGA resource mapping and routing from public tools, not an ASIC standard-cell layout or a transistor process model.
IO pins are automatically assigned. There is no board wiring contract, external IO timing constraint or hardware measurement.
The reported internal clock timing uses the nextpnr device model for this device and routing seed. It is not measured frequency or full timing signoff.
Functional proof and netlist simulation do not establish manufacturing yield, field reliability, broad CRG claims or AGI capability.

experiences.title: Commissioned racks → energy and traffic → retained work

model.identityScope: File hashes identify this exact integrated snapshot. A version label alone does not prove an unchanged implementation.

experiences.scope: A deterministic event and resource ledger for an ideally sharded fixed global GEMM-update workload. It connects admission, commissioning, power, cooling, service, checkpoint commit and restart without claiming plant design or measured productivity.
assumptions: Hardware rates, DC voltages, efficiencies, phase powers, readiness gates and faults are synthetic. Whole racks pass static feed, coolant and current bounds before dispatch.
Rack conversion losses already enter IT power. Facility PUE adds only the declared external overhead; coolant captures IT heat and must not be added again to facility energy.
Local service time is max(compute,memory); output network service is serialized by default or an explicit ideal-overlap bound. Distinct traffic interfaces do not count unique information.
Executed work equals durable plus volatile completed plus in-flight plus lost work. Retained work excludes unfinished work; only committed checkpoints survive the specified stop.
Commissioning requires all five gates. Simultaneous commit precedes fault; repair/restore and interrupted transfer bytes are retained in the ledger. No extra reliability multiplier applies.

experiences.title: Spacecraft resource budget → retained and delivered products

model.identityScope: File hashes identify this exact integrated snapshot. A version label alone does not prove an unchanged implementation.

experiences.scope: A finite-horizon synthetic spacecraft bus, radiator, product-buffer and contact ledger. It is not an orbit/attitude solution, RF link budget, flight-readiness claim or account of a current deployment.
assumptions: Sunlight and contacts are prescribed independently; a schematic orbit does not derive visibility. Solar begins at the regulated-bus boundary and array/converter thermal losses lie outside the payload radiator.
Battery efficiencies and reserve/resume hysteresis preserve energy accounting. Housekeeping has priority; bus failure discards pending work, and stored energy never becomes negative.

Radiation uses an effective isothermal emitting area and absolute kelvin. Battery losses enter heat once and RF export leaves once. Low equilibrium temperature does not establish survival or real transient behavior.

Products commit atomically before they can be delivered. Partial receiver progress survives contact closure; buffer pressure stops new work. Retained includes delivered, so those totals are not added.
Scripted resets drive work loss. Effective Poisson-rate context is not another trace multiplier or mission survival probability.
Passing declared finite-horizon targets and battery closure does not prove all future cycles, launch feasibility, replacement economics or a viable spacecraft.
